title.narrative: ILO BOUZOUR - Building inclusive markets and decent work in Lebanon
ILO BOUZOUR - inkluderande marknader och förbättrade arbetsvillkor i Libanon.

description.narrative:
1) Increased productivity and decent working conditions in the covered horticulture sector. 2) Farmers and agribusinesses connected to new market opportunities 3) Farmers enabled to use solar energy systems for electricity generation 4) Farmers and small agribusinesses capacitated to better manage their activities and resources
Final beneficiaries will be host communities and refugee workers and specifically those operating in the wider agriculture and renewable energy sectors.
Insatsens mål är att förbättra jordbrukets produktivitet, öppna upp för nya marknader för jordbruksprodukter samt att förbättra arbetsvillkoren..
The project's aim it to increase farmers' productivity, connect agri-business to new markets including decent working conditions.

Achieved results in 2024
The project supported 15 farmers (13 male, 2 female) across four cooperatives and one small agribusiness to adopt climatesmart and waterefficient technologies, for them to become models for wider replication. It improve productivity while promoting sustainability, and ensuring farmers are better equipped to cope with the challenges like water scarcity and climate variability. The groundwork laid in 2024 is designed to catalyze sectorwide adoption, with targeted outreach and capacitybuilding activities planned for 2025 to scale up these technologies and maximize their impact.
The project engaged with 21 small greenhouse manufacturers, such as welders and other service providers, to assess their readiness for further training and capacity building to better serve smallholder farmers with affordable and innovative greenhouse upgrades. These upgrades are expected to increase greenhouse productivity by an average of 50%, enhance working conditions for workers, and provide costeffective solutions for farmers. In 2025, the project plans to target at least 400 farmers to raise awareness and promote the adoption of these upgrades.
The project identified specific agricultural value chains with concrete market opportunities. The cherry value chain was targeted for its potential to drive inclusive growth, job creation, and export opportunities by extending the harvest season and enhancing product quality. The pilot saw selected SMEs bridge the gap between farmers and new markets and successfully connected with four international buyers in three countries and exporting a pilot of about 12 MT of cherries, including upgrading farmers in Aarsal to sell organic cherry to open a niche market.
The intervention engaged 145 farmers (138 male, 7 female) and 774 workers (384 female, 390 male) across three villages (Aarsal, Ainata, Kaa El Reem). Surveys indicated a 58% increase in prices obtained by farmers through intermediary cooperatives compared to the wholesale market, a 38% rise in farmers average annual incomes, and a reduction in the proportion of annual income spent on input costs from 41% to 14% between 2023 and 2024. All surveyed farmers expressed their intention to continue selling their produce through this scheme. This intervention is planned to be upscaled in 2025.
The project completed a comprehensive study on recruitment mechanisms and working conditions for workers in Lebanon's agriculture sector. The study engaged farmers, workers, intermediaries, and social partners to identify challenges and opportunities for improvement. It provided recommendations and was formally submitted to the Government of Lebanon to support national policy making. The ILO has offered technical assistance to facilitate the implementation of these recommendations. A roadmap of interventions for 2025 has been developed to enhance the recruitment systems and improving working conditions for agricultural workers.
Two roundtables engaged 26 stakeholders from the solar and agriculture sectors, showcasing best practices on successful applications of solar energy in agriculture uses. Nine solar companies and two energy associations were involved to map and promote tailored solar solutions for smallholder farmers. A prototype tool was developed to estimate solar energy needs, predesign systems, and calculate payback periods for farmers, supported by a lastmile distribution strategy to connect farmers with solar providers which will be piloted in 2025.
An intervention was conducted with portable solar rental solutions with two cooperatives to demonstrate the benefits of solar adoption for coldstorage. The cooperative reduced its energy expenses by 50%, with the cost of storage per crate of produce dropping from USD 56 to USD 33.50. Lower operational costs led to reduced storage fees for smallholder farmers, allowing more than 150 cooperative members to benefit from more affordable storage services. By reducing the usage of diesel generators, the cooperative reduced its CO2 emissions by 655kg during the pilot period. Interventions in this line continue in 2025.
